newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada spot natgas prices firm on cold weather.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot natgas prices firm on cold weather.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices firmed in Wednesday trade as temperatures in western Canada began a decline expected to last through the weekend, traders said.
Spot gas at Alberta's AECO storage hub was quoted as high as C$2.365 per gigajoule, up from C$2.281 on Tuesday. Gas for February delivery was talked at C$2.275 per GJ.

"I think we'll be in the low C$2.40s through the weekend," said a Calgary-based marketer. "It's weather driven -- it kind of has everything rocking a bit." Alberta temperatures were expected to fall to lows of -20 Celsius starting Thursday.

Marketers said storage withdrawals were at high levels with 1.35 billion cubic feet per day flowing from Alberta facilities on Tuesday. Several said they were anxious to see Friday's storage numbers from the Canadian Gas Association after a two-week period of no reporting due to the holidays.
At the borders, prices at Huntington/Sumas on the west coast were said to be in a wide range, as low as US$3.10 per million British thermal units and as high as the US$3.40s.
One British Columbia marketer said he expected prices to firm over the next few days with temperatures in the region expected to fall.

Prices at Niagara, Ontario were talked in the US$4 per mmBtu range. "It's driven more by the weather," said one marketer of eastern gas, who noted temperatures in the U.S. northeast were forecast to fall as early as Friday. "But both NYMEX and the cash are strong." ((-- Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
